title: The IKEA Effect

scenes.text: Why does stuff *you* made feel more special?
scenes.vo: Why does something you made yourself feel so much more special?

scenes.text: Scientists had people build simple IKEA boxes
scenes.vo: Scientists asked people to build simple storage boxes from IKEA. You know, the flat-pack ones.

scenes.text: Builders would pay *way more* for their own box
scenes.vo: Then they asked how much they'd pay for the box. The builders were ready to pay way more than people looking at the exact same box, already built.
This is called the IKEA effect. When you put effort into something, your brain loves it more.
But here's the twist. It only works if you finish it. Half-done projects don't get the same love.

scenes.text: Your drawing. Your Minecraft house. Your idea in a group project.
scenes.vo: It's why your own drawing, your Minecraft house, or your idea in a group project feels better than everyone else's.

scenes.text: Ask: is this really better, or did I just *work hard* on it?
scenes.vo: So ask yourself: is this really better, or did I just work hard on it?

caption:
Effort makes things feel more valuable, even a wobbly box. 🛠️ It's called the IKEA effect.

What's something you made that you're secretly super proud of? 👇
source: Norton, M. I., Mochon, D. & Ariely, D. (2012). The IKEA effect: When labor leads to love. Journal of Consumer Psychology, 22(3).
